text: Add impression-time request-context fields to the five-field Factorization Machine baseline.
rationale: The only screened feature group with positive overall and daily internal temporal-holdout lift is request_context, with full coverage and +0.002213 primary lift.
exact_ablation: Add tab, hour, and weekday as three categorical FM fields while leaving the model, BCE objective, optimizer, split, and existing five fields unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Small positive increase, approximately +0.002 to +0.004, because context can reorder impressions within users.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Small positive or flat change, approximately -0.001 to +0.003; the screening indicates weaker top-five strength than GAUC.

text: Add request context while replacing pointwise BCE with within-user RankNet pairwise loss.
rationale: Request context has measured positive screening lift, while pairwise optimization is directly aligned with within-user GAUC and can improve ordering rather than calibration.
exact_ablation: Keep the five baseline fields plus tab, hour, and weekday, and replace BCE training with within-user RankNet pairs; change no architecture or sampling policy beyond the loss implementation.

expected_effect.GAUC: Moderate positive increase, approximately +0.002 to +0.006, if valid mixed-label user groups are sufficiently common.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Small positive increase, approximately 0 to +0.004, with less certainty because RankNet is not explicitly top-five weighted.

text: Add request context and use a BCE plus nDCG@5-weighted pairwise hybrid objective.
rationale: The measured request-context signal is positive, while the hybrid objective specifically targets the observed weakness in top-five ranking without discarding BCE stability.
exact_ablation: Keep the baseline FM and add tab, hour, and weekday; replace BCE with BCE plus a fixed-weight within-group nDCG@5-swap-weighted pairwise term.

expected_effect.GAUC: Small to moderate positive increase, approximately +0.001 to +0.004, because pairwise corrections should preserve broad ordering.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Moderate positive increase, approximately +0.002 to +0.007, if training groups approximate evaluated candidate groups.

text: Add request context and replace the FM scorer with an embedding-plus-MLP scorer using the same eligible fields.
rationale: Request context is the only positively screened feature group; an MLP may capture nonlinear user/item/context interactions that the shallow FM misses while using no additional unavailable features.
exact_ablation: Use the same five baseline fields plus tab, hour, and weekday, but replace the FM interaction scorer with a small embedding-plus-MLP scorer; keep pointwise BCE and the data split unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Small positive increase, approximately +0.001 to +0.005, if nonlinear context interactions improve within-user ordering.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Small positive or flat change, approximately -0.001 to +0.004, because extra capacity may improve general ordering without reliably fixing top-five errors.

text: Add request context and replace the FM scorer with a low-rank Deep & Cross ranker.
rationale: The measured context lift suggests interactions with identity fields matter; a bounded cross branch is a targeted architectural change rather than an unrestricted large model.
exact_ablation: Use the baseline five fields plus tab, hour, and weekday, and replace the FM scorer with one low-rank two-layer cross branch over field embeddings; retain pointwise BCE and all training settings.

expected_effect.GAUC: Small positive increase, approximately +0.001 to +0.004, from explicit context-by-identity interactions.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Small positive or flat change, approximately -0.001 to +0.004; overfitting rare combinations could reduce top-five quality.

text: Add request context and use group-complete, stratified minibatches while retaining the baseline FM and BCE loss.
rationale: The request-context signal is positive but modest relative to daily variability; preserving complete candidate groups during training can make ordering supervision more consistent without introducing new features.
exact_ablation: Keep the baseline FM, five fields plus request context, BCE loss, and optimizer unchanged, but change row minibatching to group-complete stratified minibatches.

expected_effect.GAUC: Small positive increase, approximately +0.0005 to +0.003, if partial groups currently dilute within-user comparisons.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Small positive or flat change, approximately -0.001 to +0.003, with sensitivity to the realized group distribution.

text: Add request context and use a lower learning rate with longer patience for the same FM and BCE model.
rationale: The context screening is consistently positive across dates but has substantial daily variance, so a more conservative optimization schedule may retain stable context interactions instead of selecting an unstable checkpoint.
exact_ablation: Add tab, hour, and weekday and change only the learning rate from 0.001 to 0.0005 with patience increased from 4 to 8; retain architecture, loss, batch size, and maximum epochs otherwise.

expected_effect.GAUC: Small positive increase, approximately 0 to +0.003, if the baseline underfits or overshoots context interactions.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Flat to small positive change, approximately -0.001 to +0.002; slower optimization may not improve top-five ordering.

text: Add request context and increase FM interaction dimension from 16 to 32.
rationale: Request context shows positive measured lift, and a larger interaction space may represent its interactions with user, video, author, tab, and duration more completely.
exact_ablation: Add tab, hour, and weekday and change only the FM interaction dimension from 16 to 32; keep pointwise BCE, optimizer, regularization, fields, and schedule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Small positive increase, approximately 0 to +0.003, if the original interaction rank is capacity-limited.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Flat to small positive change, approximately -0.001 to +0.003; additional capacity may overfit sparse combinations.

text: Add request context and apply stronger embedding regularization in the baseline FM.
rationale: The context gain is positive but noisy, so regularization is a bounded way to reduce memorization of rare context-by-ID combinations while retaining the measured feature family.
exact_ablation: Add tab, hour, and weekday and change only FM embedding L2 from 1e-6 to 1e-5; keep weights, architecture, BCE, and schedule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Small positive or flat change, approximately -0.001 to +0.003, with benefit if rare interactions currently overfit.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Small positive or flat change, approximately -0.001 to +0.003; excessive shrinkage could hurt top-five separation.

text: Add request context and use separate embeddings for hour and weekday rather than treating context as one combined token.
rationale: The measured group is full-coverage and positive on every screened date; factorizing its components can generalize context effects across users and items better than a single high-cardinality conjunction.
exact_ablation: Add tab, hour, and weekday as independent FM fields with separate vocabularies and embeddings, rather than one concatenated request-context token; change no other field, loss, or training setting.

expected_effect.GAUC: Small positive increase, approximately +0.001 to +0.004, from better sharing across repeated temporal contexts.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Small positive increase, approximately 0 to +0.003, unless the task requires highly specific joint context combinations.

text: Add request context and use balanced positive weighting in the baseline BCE objective.
rationale: Request context has positive measured ranking lift, while increasing positive-loss emphasis may improve separation of long-view impressions when the natural label distribution is highly imbalanced.
exact_ablation: Add tab, hour, and weekday and change only BCE to use a fixed positive-class weight of 2.0; retain the FM, fields, optimizer, schedule, and evaluation distribution unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Small positive or flat change, approximately -0.001 to +0.003, because class weighting can alter score ordering but is not directly pairwise.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Flat to small positive change, approximately -0.002 to +0.003; excessive positive weighting can promote false positives into the top five.

text: Add request context and use two independent FM interaction blocks whose logits are averaged.
rationale: The context family has measured positive lift, but its daily variability suggests a small ensemble may reduce seed-specific interaction noise without adding any disallowed signal.
exact_ablation: Add tab, hour, and weekday and replace the single FM with an average of two independently seeded identical FM models; change no features, loss, optimizer, or data policy.

expected_effect.GAUC: Small positive increase, approximately 0 to +0.003, from reduced estimation variance across sparse interactions.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Flat to small positive change, approximately -0.001 to +0.003; averaging can soften useful high-confidence top-five scores.
